question:
How should test inputs be chosen for a function that accepts numeric values within a valid range?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

When testing a function that accepts numeric values within a valid range, test inputs should be selected using equivalence partitioning to cover valid and invalid classes, boundary value analysis to target extreme values, robustness testing for out-of-range inputs, and exception/combinatorial techniques to ensure comprehensive coverage.

# Guidelines

- Partition the input domain into equivalence classes based on valid and invalid inputs; select a representative test case from each class. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing Methodologies and Techniques/Boundary Value Analysis and Syntax Testing Techniques.md)

- Choose test cases [SWEBOK excerpt bb061752587bc7b35163], as [SWEBOK excerpt 44266d1663bca03e93fd]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing Methodologies and Techniques/Boundary Value Analysis and Syntax Testing Techniques.md)

- Include test cases outside the valid input domain (robustness testing) to verify the function handles unexpected or erroneous inputs appropriately. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing Methodologies and Techniques/Boundary Value Analysis and Syntax Testing Techniques.md)

- Include out-of-range values that may [SWEBOK excerpt 87d891290de2e929007d] as part of the test suite. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing Methodologies and Techniques/Boundary Value Analysis and Syntax Testing Techniques.md)

- Design test cases specifically to check whether the function can manage predefined exceptions such as overflow or underflow, focusing on negative test scenarios that force error messages. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Testing Approaches and Execution Strategies/Software Testing Techniques and Methodologies/Exception Testing and Error Handling in Software Testing.md)

- Use combinatorial test techniques to systematically derive test cases covering specific parameter values or conditions across the valid range. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing Methodologies and Techniques/Combinatorial Test Techniques Overview.md)

- Supplement structured input selection with randomly generated test cases within the input domain to broaden coverage. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Testing Approaches and Execution Strategies/Scenario-Based and Random Testing Approaches.md)
